messages.subject: R-INLA model crashing
parts:
Hello, 

A model I am running on a large dataset (116,000 rows) is crashing with the following error:

sh: line 1:  7875 Aborted                 '/home/meisnerj/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.6/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.run' -b -s -v -t 4 '/state/partition1/scratch/37063.1.student.q/RtmpqWHiBX/file1de0775e1eff/Model.ini' > '/state/partition1/scratch/37063.1.student.q/RtmpqWHiBX/file1de0775e1eff/Logfile.txt'

It runs fine when I use a different offset (two different methods for estimating population). 

Any suggestions you have would be welcome. 

Thanks,
Julianne

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R-INLA model crashing
parts:
I would guess that something in the model is badly scaled, so a slight change can tip it over the edge to get and Inf / NA 

If you only change the offset, then if

r = inla(...)

runs fine, the change the offset and run it again using

rr = inla(...., control.mode=list(result=r, restart=T))

Let me know
H

Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R-INLA model crashing
parts:
Thank you. 

I'm assuming here that r is the successful run, not the run that exited with error? My goal is to run the same model but with WorldPop population estimates as the offset in one model, and LandScan as the offset in another. 

I believe you're suggesting I do this:

rW=inla(..., offset=log(WorldPop))#rW exits with error

rL=inla(..., offset=log(LandScan))#rL runs successfully

rr=inla(..., offset=log(WorldPop), control.mode=list(result=rL, restart=T))

Is that correct?

Note in another iteration of the model, it ran fine with the WorldPop offset, but produced the same error with LandScan, but for each model iteration at least one of the two worked (but that won't help with my goal of comparing the two :)). Not sure if that is helpful?

Thanks,
Julianne
